title.en: The physical layer: how bits travel on the wire
title.zh: 物理层：比特怎样在线上走

description.en: Work out what the bits sent by the browser actually are in cable, fibre and air, how fast, how long and how far they go, which medium carries them, and how bits become signals and are recovered again.
description.zh: 弄清浏览器发出的比特在线缆、光纤和空气里是什么，走多快、多久、多远，靠什么载体，以及比特怎样变成信号、又怎样被还原。

name.en: What the physical layer does: the link model
name.zh: 物理层管什么：链路模型 (what the physical layer does; the link model)

name.en: Bandwidth and latency: transmission delay and propagation delay
name.zh: 带宽与延迟：传输延迟和传播延迟 (bandwidth, transmission delay, propagation delay, latency)

name.en: Copper cable and signal attenuation: twisted pair, coaxial cable
name.zh: 有线铜缆与信号衰减 (twisted pair, coaxial cable, signal attenuation)

name.en: Wireless transmission and EM waves: the spectrum
name.zh: 无线传输与电磁波 (wireless transmission, EM waves, spectrum)

name.en: Sending data with signals: the three parameters of a sine wave
name.zh: 用信号传数据：正弦波的三个参数 (data communication using signals)
数字调制：基带与通带 (digital modulation, baseband vs passband)

name.en: Sampling and reconstruction: sample at least twice the highest frequency
name.zh: 采样与重建：采样率至少两倍最高频率 (sampling and reconstruction)
码元速率与数据速率 (symbol rate and data rate)

description.en: Treating bandwidth in bit/s and bandwidth in Hz as the same thing; the first is how many bits are sent per second, the second is the range of frequencies a signal occupies.
description.zh: 把 bit/s 的带宽和 Hz 的带宽当成同一个东西；前者是每秒传多少比特，后者是信号占的频率范围。

description.en: Thinking that a fatter pipe makes a long distance faster; propagation delay depends only on distance and signal speed, and bandwidth cannot change it.
description.zh: 以为把带宽加粗，远距离就会变快；传播延迟只由距离和信号速度决定，带宽改变不了它。

description.en: Treating latency as propagation time only, forgetting that pushing the whole message onto the link also takes time.
description.zh: 把延迟只当成传播时间，忘了把整条消息推上链路也要时间。

description.en: Treating the baud rate (symbol rate) and the bit rate as the same thing; they are equal only when each symbol carries 1 bit.
description.zh: 把波特率（码元速率）和比特率当成一回事；只有每个码元带 1 个比特时两者才相等。

description.en: Thinking that a sampling rate equal to the signal frequency is enough; it must be at least twice the highest frequency, otherwise aliasing appears.
description.zh: 以为采样率等于信号频率就够了；至少要两倍于最高频率，否则出现混叠。

description.en: Thinking GEO satellite internet is slow because its bandwidth is small; its delay comes mainly from the speed of light and the 36,000 km distance.
description.zh: 以为 GEO 卫星上网慢是因为带宽小；它的延迟主要来自光速和 3.6 万公里的距离。

title.en: The HTTPS request reaches the wire
title.zh: HTTPS 请求到了线上

prompt.en: Your laptop has wrapped the HTTPS request layer by layer and handed it to layer 1 (the physical layer). What is it that actually travels in the cable, fibre or air?
prompt.zh: 你的笔记本把 HTTPS 请求一层层封装好，交给第 1 层（物理层）。在线缆、光纤或空气里真正跑的，是什么？

label.en: Pieces of text, like sending a telegram
label.zh: 一段一段的文字，像发电报

feedback.en: Wire and air do not know text; they only know changes in physical quantities such as voltage, light and the electromagnetic field.
feedback.zh: 线和空气不认识文字，只认得电压、光、电磁场这些物理量的变化。

label.en: A string of 0s and 1s, turned into changes in voltage, light pulses or radio waves
label.zh: 一串 0 和 1 的比特，被变成电压、光脉冲或无线电波的变化

label.en: Whole packets, with addresses on the wire too
label.zh: 一个个完整的分组，线上也带着地址

feedback.en: Addresses are in the layer 3 header; by the physical layer they are just part of the bits. There is no such thing as a “packet” on the wire.
feedback.zh: 地址是第 3 层头里的内容，到了物理层，它只是比特的一部分。线上没有『分组』这种东西。

explain.en: The physical layer’s job is to turn bits into something that can travel in a medium, and turn them back into bits at the other end. That is what this lesson is about.
explain.zh: 物理层的任务，就是把比特变成能在介质里走的东西，到另一头再变回比特。这一课讲的就是这件事。

title.en: The physical layer does three things; see the wire as a pipe
title.zh: 物理层管三件事，把线看成一根管子

text.en: Slide 2 asks: where is the physical layer in the OSI model? And in the TCP/IP model? Following on from the last lesson: it is layer 1 of OSI and also layer 1 of the five layers in this course; TCP/IP merges it with the data link layer into one link layer, so in TCP/IP it is the lower half of the link layer.
text.zh: 课件第 2 页问：物理层在 OSI 模型的哪里？在 TCP/IP 模型里呢？接上上一课：它是 OSI 的第 1 层，也是本课程五层里的第 1 层；TCP/IP 把它和数据链路层并成了一个链路层，所以在 TCP/IP 里，它是链路层的下半部分。

text.en: The physical layer deals with three kinds of **interface**. The slides sum them up in three words, and behind each word is a class of practical problems.
text.zh: 物理层管的是网络的三种**接口**，课件用三个词概括，每个词后面都是一类实际问题。

rows.en: How signals are represented: voltage, signal strength
rows.zh: 信号怎样表示：电压、信号强度

rows.en: How many volts mean 1? How are light and radio waves represented?
rows.zh: 用多少伏代表 1？光和电波怎样表示？

rows.en: The last part: signals, modulation, sampling, symbol rate
rows.zh: 最后一部分：信号、调制、采样、码元速率

rows.en: How fast, how long: the data rate
How many bits per second? How long until a message arrives?
rows.zh: 一秒发多少比特？消息多久到？

rows.en: Copper, fibre or air? How far at most?
rows.zh: 用铜线、光纤还是空气？最长多远？

rows.en: Transmission media: copper, fibre, wireless, satellite
rows.zh: 传输介质：铜缆、光纤、无线、卫星

text.en: To keep the problem simple at first, the slides abstract all of this into a **link**: a “pipe” $L$ metres long, with bits put in at one end and coming out unchanged at the other.
text.zh: 为了先把问题讲简单，课件把这些全部抽象成一条**链路** (link)：一根长 $L$ 米的『管子』，一头放进比特，另一头原样出来。

alt.zh: 浏览器和服务器各有 HTTPS、TCP、IP、PHY 四层，PHY 之间用一根长 L 米的管子相连，管子里流动着 10111 这样的比特

caption.zh: 课件第 4 页的链路模型

text.en: This has a big advantage: the layers above need not care whether the wire is copper, light or air. **But the simplification also drops things**:
text.zh: 这样画有一个大好处：上面几层完全不用关心线是铜的、光的，还是空气。**但这个简化也丢掉了东西**：

items.en: Signals weaken on the wire and are disturbed, so bits can be wrong (handled in lessons 5 and 6).
items.zh: 信号在线上会变弱、会被干扰，比特可能出错（第 5、6 课处理）。

items.en: A wire may be shared by several machines, which have to contend for it (lesson 7).
items.zh: 线可能是好几台机器共用的，要争（第 7 课）。

items.en: A signal takes time to cross the wire, and the pipe has a thickness too: there is a limit to how many bits can be poured in per second.
items.zh: 信号走过这条线要花时间，管子也有粗细：一秒灌得进多少比特，有上限。

text.en: So from here on we keep just two numbers for the pipe: its **thickness** (bandwidth) and its **length** (delay).
text.zh: 所以后面我们给这根管子只留两个数：**粗细**（带宽）和**长短**（延迟）。

title.en: Bandwidth: how thick the pipe is
title.zh: 带宽：管子有多粗

text.en: **Bandwidth** is the transmission rate of a link: how many bits it can carry per second, in bit/s (bits per second). Think of the link as a water pipe, and bandwidth is how thick the pipe is: the thicker, the more goes in per unit time. 10 Mbit/s means ten million bits per second.
text.zh: **带宽** (bandwidth) 是链路的传输速率：每秒能传多少比特，单位是 bit/s（bits per second）。把链路看成水管，带宽就是管子的粗细：越粗，单位时间灌进去的越多。10 Mbit/s 就是每秒一千万个比特。

text.en: Numbers get big, so we use prefixes. First, the values of the words in the box on slide 6:
text.zh: 数字一大，就要用前缀。课件第 6 页框里的那几个词，先把它们的值写出来：

text.en: Bandwidth is measured in bits, while file sizes are often in bytes; 1 byte = 8 bits. Don’t forget the 8 when converting.
text.zh: 带宽用的是比特 (bit)，文件大小常用字节 (byte)，1 字节 = 8 比特。换算的时候别漏了这个 8。

title.en: Two kinds of “bandwidth”
title.zh: 两个『带宽』

body.en: The bandwidth on this page is “bits per second” (bit/s). Later, when we get to cables, you will see “twisted pair 16 MHz, coaxial close to 1 GHz”; there, bandwidth is the **range of frequencies** a signal occupies, in hertz (Hz). The two are related: the wider the range of frequencies a wire lets through, the higher the bit rate it can usually carry, and the B in the next lesson’s channel capacity formula is in Hz. When you read “bandwidth”, check the unit first: bit/s or Hz.
body.zh: 这一页的带宽，是『每秒多少比特』(bit/s)。再往后讲线缆，会看到『双绞线 16 MHz、同轴接近 1 GHz』，那里的带宽，是信号占的**频率范围**，单位是赫兹 (Hz)。两者有关系：线能放行的频率范围越宽，能传的比特速率往往越高，下一课信道容量公式里的 B 就是 Hz。读到『带宽』，先看单位：bit/s，还是 Hz。

title.en: How many phone calls can one fibre carry at once
title.zh: 一根光纤能同时打多少个电话

intro.en: Slide 6: one voice call needs about 1 kbit/s, and a single-mode fibre can reach 1 Tbit/s. How many calls can one fibre carry at once? First write “packing portions into the pipe” as a division, then convert the units to the same kind.
intro.zh: 课件第 6 页：一路语音约需 1 kbit/s，单模光纤的带宽可达 1 Tbit/s。一根光纤能同时传多少路电话？先把『一份一份装进管子』写成除法，再把单位换成同一种。

why.en: Each call takes one portion of the bandwidth; the number of portions that fit in the pipe is the total bandwidth divided by the bandwidth of one portion.
why.zh: 每路电话占一份带宽，管子里能装几份，就是总带宽除以每份的带宽。

why.en: tera is $10^{12}$ and kilo is $10^{3}$. Convert both to bit/s first so the units cancel.
why.zh: tera 是 $10^{12}$，kilo 是 $10^{3}$。先都换成 bit/s，单位才能约掉。

why.en: When dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents. The answer is a billion calls.
why.zh: 同底的幂相除，指数相减。答案是十亿路。

outro.en: The slide’s 1 kbit/s is a rough teaching value. A real digital phone call usually uses 64 kbit/s, in which case $N = 10^{12} \div (64 \times 10^{3}) \approx 1.6 \times 10^{7}$, about 15.6 million calls. The order of magnitude is still staggering: the bandwidth of one fibre is worth over ten million phone calls.
outro.zh: 课件取 1 kbit/s 是教学用的粗略值。真实的数字电话常用 64 kbit/s，这时 $N = 10^{12} \div (64 \times 10^{3}) \approx 1.6 \times 10^{7}$，约 1560 万路。数量级依然惊人：一根光纤的带宽，抵得上千万路电话。

title.en: Latency: first fill the bucket, then wait for the water to flow through
title.zh: 延迟：先灌满桶，再等水流过去

text.en: Bandwidth says “how much can be sent in a second”, but not “how long until it arrives”. Look at one more thing: how long it takes in total to send a message from A to B. This time is called **latency**.
text.zh: 带宽说的是『一秒能送多少』，但没说『多久能到』。再看一件事：把一条消息从 A 送到 B，总共要多久。这个时间叫**延迟** (latency)。

text.en: Think of a water pipe. Getting a bucket of water from one end of the pipe to the other takes two stretches of time: first **pour** the whole bucket into the pipe, which takes longer the bigger the bucket and the narrower the opening; then the water **flows through** the pipe, which takes longer the longer the pipe and the slower the flow. The two happen one after the other, so they add.
text.zh: 用水管来想。要把一桶水从管子这头送到那头，时间分两段：先把整桶水**灌进**管子，桶越大、管口越细，灌得越久；然后水在管子里**流过去**，管子越长、水流越慢，越久。两段先后发生，所以相加。

alt.en: Timeline: first time T pushes all the message’s bits onto the link, then time P lets the last bit cross the link; the total latency is the sum of the two
alt.zh: 时间轴：先用时间 T 把整条消息的比特推上链路，再用时间 P 让最后一个比特走完链路，总延迟是两者之和

caption.en: After the last bit is pushed onto the link, it still has to travel the whole way
caption.zh: 最后一个比特推上链路之后，还要走完全程

items.en: **Transmission delay** (T-delay): the time needed to push all of the message’s bits onto the link; it depends on **how long the message is and how fast the rate is**: $T = \dfrac{\text{bits in the message}}{\text{transmission rate}}$.
items.zh: **传输延迟** (transmission delay, T-delay)：把整条消息的比特推上链路所需的时间，看**消息多长、速率多快**：$T = \dfrac{\text{消息的比特数}}{\text{传输速率}}$。

items.en: **Propagation delay** (P-delay): the time one bit needs to travel the whole link; it depends on **how far and how fast the signal is**: $P = \dfrac{\text{link length}}{\text{signal speed}}$. In a wire the signal speed is about $\frac{2}{3}$ of the speed of light $C$, where $C = 300\,000$ km/s.
items.zh: **传播延迟** (propagation delay, P-delay)：一个比特在链路里走完全程所需的时间，看**距离多远、信号多快**：$P = \dfrac{\text{链路长度}}{\text{信号速度}}$。导线里信号速度约为光速 $C$ 的 $\frac{2}{3}$，$C = 300\,000$ km/s。

text.en: Why add? At the moment the last bit has been pushed onto the link, T has already passed; it still has to travel the whole way, and after another P the whole message has arrived.
text.zh: 为什么相加？最后一个比特被推上链路的那一刻，已经过去了 T；它还得走完全程，再过 P，才算整条消息到齐。

text.en: Which of the two dominates depends on the case: for a **small message on a long route**, T is almost zero and P is the larger part; for a **big file on a short route**, P is tiny and T is the larger part.
text.zh: 两个时间谁说了算，要看情形：**小消息跑远路**，T 几乎为零，P 占大头；**大文件走近路**，P 很小，T 占大头。

title.en: The slides use different names
title.zh: 课件里叫法不一

body.en: The “delay” on slide 5 means the time for the first bit to go from A to B, that is, the propagation delay; the “latency” on slide 7 means the total time of the whole message, equal to T plus P. The formulas say message and the examples say frame: to the physical layer they are both “a string of bits to send”, and “frame” is the name layer 2 gives it. In exams, latency = T-delay + P-delay.
body.zh: 第 5 页的 delay 指第一个比特从 A 走到 B 的时间，也就是传播延迟；第 7 页的 latency 指整条消息的总时间，等于 T 加 P。公式里说 message，例题里说 frame：对物理层来说它们都是『要发的一串比特』，frame 是第 2 层给它起的名字。考试里，latency = T-delay + P-delay。

title.en: Two problems: a 56 Kbps modem, and fibre across the country
title.zh: 做两题：56 Kbps 的调制解调器，和横跨全国的光纤

intro.en: The two problems on slides 8 and 9 come without answers. We work them together and write the units clearly: Kbps converted to bit/s, and signal speed and distance both in km and km/s.
intro.zh: 课件第 8、9 页的两道题没有给答案。我们一起算，并把单位写清楚：Kbps 换成 bit/s，信号速度和距离统一用 km 和 km/s。

why.en: Problem 1: 56 Kbps = 56 000 bit/s, and the frame is 5600 bits. Pushing it out takes 0.1 s, that is 100 milliseconds.
why.zh: 第一题：56 Kbps = 56 000 bit/s，帧 5600 比特。推完要 0.1 秒，也就是 100 毫秒。

why.en: The problem says the signal speed is $\frac{2}{3}C$.
Distance 5 km divided by the speed gives 25 microseconds ($1\ \mu\text{s} = 10^{-6}$ s). T is 4000 times P: on a slow, short line, pushing the bits is the main part.
why.zh: 距离 5 km 除以速度，得 25 微秒（$1\ \mu\text{s} = 10^{-6}$ s）。T 比 P 大 4000 倍：慢速短线上，推比特是大头。

why.en: Problem 2: 100 Mbps = $10^{8}$ bit/s, and the frame is still 5600 bits.
why.zh: 第二题：100 Mbps = $10^{8}$ bit/s，帧还是 5600 比特。

why.en: In this problem the signal speed is taken as $C$. In reality light in fibre travels at about $\frac{2}{3}C$, in which case P is about 5 ms.
why.zh: 这一题题设信号速度取 $C$。现实里光在光纤中约为 $\frac{2}{3}C$，那时 P 约为 5 ms。

why.en: On a fast, long line, propagation is the main part: 3.33 ms is about 60 times 56 µs.
why.zh: 快而长的线上，传播是大头：3.33 ms 约是 56 µs 的 60 倍。

outro.en: The two problems reach opposite conclusions: **with a slow rate and a short distance, transmission delay decides; with a fast rate and a long distance, propagation delay decides.** So for a small message on a long route look at propagation, and for a big file on a short route look at transmission. One more thing: to make a long distance faster, making the bandwidth fatter does not help, because P depends only on distance and signal speed.
outro.zh: 两题的结论正好相反：**速率慢、距离短，传输延迟说了算；速率快、距离长，传播延迟说了算。** 所以，小消息跑远路看传播，大文件走近路看传输。还有一件事：想让远距离更快，把带宽加粗没用，因为 P 只由距离和信号速度决定。

title.en: Work out the latency of a link
title.zh: 算一条链路的延迟

prompt.en: A 10 Mbps link is 200 km long, and the signal speed is taken as $\frac{2}{3}C$ (C = 300 000 km/s). A 12 000-bit frame is to be sent. From the moment the first bit is pushed out until the last bit arrives at the far end, how many milliseconds does it take in total?
prompt.zh: 一条 10 Mbps 的链路长 200 km，信号速度取 $\frac{2}{3}C$（C = 300 000 km/s）。要发一个 12 000 比特的帧，从第一个比特推出，到最后一个比特到达对面，一共要多少毫秒？

hints.en: First work out T and P separately, convert both to milliseconds, then add.
hints.zh: 先分别算 T 和 P，单位都换成毫秒再相加。

explain.en: T = 12 000 ÷ 10^7 = 1.2 ms. Signal speed = 200 000 km/s, so P = 200 ÷ 200 000 = 1 ms. Total latency = 2.2 ms. The two are about the same size here; if the link is changed to 1 Gbps, T becomes 0.012 ms and P is still 1 ms, so propagation decides.
explain.zh: T = 12 000 ÷ 10^7 = 1.2 ms。信号速度 = 200 000 km/s，P = 200 ÷ 200 000 = 1 ms。总延迟 = 2.2 ms。这里两者差不多大；如果把链路换成 1 Gbps，T 变成 0.012 ms，P 仍是 1 ms，就是传播说了算。

chapter.en: Transmission media: wire, light and air

title.en: Why are two wires twisted together
title.zh: 两根线为什么要拧在一起

prompt.en: The copper wires in a network cable (twisted pair) always come in pairs twisted like a rope. What do you think twisting them together is for?
prompt.zh: 网线（双绞线）里的铜线总是成对地拧成麻花。你觉得拧在一起是为了什么？

label.en: To make the cable stronger and harder to snap
label.zh: 让线更结实，不容易拉断

feedback.en: Strength is a side benefit, not the reason it exists.
feedback.zh: 结实是附带的好处，不是它存在的理由。

label.en: To make outside electromagnetic interference almost the same on both wires, so it cancels at the receiving end
label.zh: 让外界的电磁干扰对两根线几乎一样，在接收端相互抵消

label.en: To make the signal travel faster
label.zh: 让信号走得更快

feedback.en: The speed of a signal in copper has almost nothing to do with whether it is twisted.
feedback.zh: 信号在铜线里的速度和拧不拧基本无关。

explain.en: The answer is b. The next page first covers why signals weaken, then comes back to this.
explain.zh: 答案是 b。下一页先说信号为什么会变弱，再回到这里。

title.en: Copper cable: attenuation, twisted pair and coaxial
title.zh: 铜缆：衰减、双绞线和同轴

text.en: Signals weaken: attenuation
text.zh: 信号会变弱：衰减

text.en: A signal passing through any medium gets smaller in amplitude; this is **attenuation**. The longer the wire, the weaker the signal; once it is so weak that the receiver cannot tell it from background noise, that stretch is unusable. So attenuation decides **how far** and **how much** a medium can carry. The fix is a **repeater** every so often: it takes in the weakened signal, cleans it up, and sends it out again with enough strength.
text.zh: 信号穿过任何介质，幅度都会变小，这叫**衰减** (attenuation)。线越长，信号越弱；弱到接收方分不清它和背景噪声，这一段就不能用了。所以衰减决定了一种介质**能传多远**、**能传多少**。办法是每隔一段放一个**中继器** (repeater)：把变弱的信号收下，整理好，再用足够的力量重新发出去。

alt.zh: 一段正弦信号向右走，幅度越来越小；经过中继器后幅度恢复，再向右走又逐渐变小

caption.en: A repeater regenerates the weakened signal
caption.zh: 中继器把变弱的信号再生出来

text.en: Attenuation is often measured in **decibels** (dB):
text.zh: 衰减常用**分贝** (dB) 来量：

text.en: $P_{\text{in}}$ is the power going in and $P_{\text{out}}$ the power coming out. Half the power left is about 3 dB; $\frac{1}{100}$ left is 20 dB. The advantage of logarithms is that when several stretches of wire are joined, their attenuation in decibels simply adds. Attenuation also depends on frequency: on copper the higher the frequency, the greater the attenuation, which is why wires come in grades.
text.zh: $P_{\text{in}}$ 是进去的功率，$P_{\text{out}}$ 是出来的功率。功率剩一半，约是 3 dB；剩 $\frac{1}{100}$，就是 20 dB。用对数的好处是：几段线连起来，衰减的分贝数可以直接相加。衰减还和频率有关，铜线上频率越高，衰减越厉害，这也是为什么线要分等级。

text.en: Twisted pair
text.zh: 双绞线

text.en: **Twisted pair**: two insulated copper wires wound into a spiral, the coloured wires inside a network cable. Why twist them? Outside electromagnetic interference (nearby power lines, motors) induces noise in a wire. If the two wires are close together and take turns being nearer the source, the noise on the two wires is almost equal. The receiving end does not look at the voltage of each wire, only at the **difference between the two**: equal noise subtracts away, while the real signal (one wire high, the other low) is actually doubled. The tighter the twist and the better the wire, the cleaner the cancellation and the higher the usable frequency.
text.zh: **双绞线** (twisted pair)：两根绝缘的铜线，绕成螺旋，就是网线里那几对彩色线。为什么要拧？外界的电磁干扰（旁边的电线、电机）会在线里感应出杂波。如果两根线挨得近，又轮流靠近干扰源，杂波落在两根线上几乎一样大。接收端不看每根线的电压，只看**两根线的差**：相同的杂波相减，抵消了；真正的信号（一根线高、另一根线低）反而被加倍。拧得越密、线质越好，抵消得越干净，能用的频率就越高。

text.en: Twisted pair is used in Ethernet. Its bandwidth (here in Hz, not bit/s) depends on distance, wire quality and how tightly it is twisted: Cat 3 is about 16 MHz and Cat 8 about 2 GHz. The slides say the distance can reach 5 km, extended with repeaters when needed.
text.zh: 双绞线用在以太网里。它的带宽（这里是 Hz，不是 bit/s）取决于距离、线的质量和缠绕的密度：Cat 3 约 16 MHz，Cat 8 约 2 GHz。课件写距离可达 5 km，需要时用中继器延长。

title.en: Beyond the slides
title.zh: 超出课件

body.en: 5 km is closer to the figure for telephone lines. A stretch of twisted pair used for Ethernet is usually only about 100 metres; farther than that you switch to fibre or add equipment in between. Putting the two numbers side by side easily gives the impression that an Ethernet cable can run 5 km.
body.zh: 5 km 更接近电话线的数字。以太网用的双绞线，一段通常只有约 100 米，更远就要换光纤，或者中间加设备。这两个数字放在一起，容易让人以为以太网线能拉 5 km。

text.en: Coaxial cable
text.zh: 同轴电缆

text.en: **Coaxial cable**: a copper core in the middle, and around it in turn an insulating layer, a layer of braided copper mesh (the shield) and a plastic jacket. The mesh acts like a cover that separates the core from the outside: interference from outside cannot get in, and the signal inside cannot leak out. So it can run at higher speeds over longer distances than twisted pair, with a bandwidth close to 1 GHz, and it is still used today for cable TV and internet over cable TV.
text.zh: **同轴电缆** (coaxial cable)：中间一根铜芯，外面依次是绝缘层、一层编织的铜网（屏蔽层）、塑料外皮。铜网像一个罩子，把铜芯和外界隔开：外面的干扰进不来，里面的信号也漏不出去。所以它比双绞线能在更远的距离上跑更高的速度，带宽接近 1 GHz，今天仍用在有线电视和有线电视上网。

title.en: Fibre: locking light in a glass thread
title.zh: 光纤：把光锁在一根玻璃丝里

text.en: The trouble with copper is that once the signal gets weak or messy, it cannot go far. Fibre takes a different approach: it uses light, not electricity.
text.zh: 铜线的毛病，是信号一弱、一乱，就走不远。光纤换了个办法：不用电，用光。

text.en: **Fibre optics** sends data as light pulses through a thin glass thread. Its bandwidth is extremely high (on the order of THz) and the signal loss is very small, so it suits backbone networks and fibre to the home. The system has three parts: a **light source** (an LED or a semiconductor laser), a **transmission medium** (glass fibre) and a **detector** (which produces an electrical pulse when light hits it). How are bits encoded? The simplest convention: **light = 1, no light = 0**.
text.zh: **光纤** (fibre optics) 用光脉冲，通过一根细玻璃丝传数据。它的带宽极高（THz 量级），信号损失又很小，所以适合骨干网和光纤到户。系统有三部分：**光源**（LED 或半导体激光器）、**传输介质**（玻璃纤维）、**探测器**（光一照到就产生电脉冲）。比特怎么编码？最简单的约定：**有光 = 1，无光 = 0**。

caption.en: The three parts of a fibre, and multimode versus single-mode
caption.zh: 光纤的三部分，以及多模与单模的区别

text.en: Why light does not leak out: total internal reflection
text.zh: 光为什么不会漏出去：全内反射

text.en: When light passes from one medium into another, its direction bends; this is refraction. The **core** of a fibre is glass with a higher refractive index, wrapped in a **cladding** with a slightly lower index, and outermost is a plastic **jacket**. When light goes from the core towards the cladding and hits the boundary at a shallow enough angle (a small angle to the boundary), it does not get out but bounces almost entirely back into the core; this is **total internal reflection**. Bouncing like this all the way, the light is locked in the glass thread. When the slides say “refraction at the air–glass interface is compensated in the design”, they mean: the refraction when light enters through the end face has already been accounted for in the design, which guarantees that the light entering hits the core–cladding boundary at an angle that gives total internal reflection.
text.zh: 光从一种介质进入另一种介质，方向会拐弯，这叫折射。光纤的**纤芯** (core) 是折射率较高的玻璃，外面包着折射率略低的**包层** (cladding)，最外面是塑料**外套** (jacket)。光从纤芯射向包层时，如果射到界面时足够『擦边』（与界面夹角小），就不会钻出去，而是几乎完全反弹回纤芯，这叫**全内反射** (total internal reflection)。就这样一路弹着前进，光被锁在玻璃丝里。课件说『空气和玻璃界面的折射在设计上被补偿』，意思是：光从端面射入时的折射，设计时已经算进去了，保证进去的光射到纤芯和包层的界面时，角度正好能发生全内反射。

text.en: Single-mode and multimode
text.zh: 单模和多模

items.en: **Multimode fibre**: the core is about 50 µm, fairly thick, and light can bounce along many paths. Used with cheap LEDs, for cheap short distances, such as 300 to 550 m.
items.zh: **多模光纤** (multi-mode)：纤芯约 50 µm，比较粗，光可以沿多条路径弹着走。配便宜的 LED，用于便宜的短距离，如 300 至 550 m。

items.en: **Single-mode fibre**: the core is very thin, about 10 µm, and light basically has just one straight path left, with no room even to bounce. Used with lasers, for long distances of 10 to 200 km.
items.zh: **单模光纤** (single-mode)：纤芯很细，约 10 µm，光基本只剩一条直路可走，连反弹的余地都没有。配激光器，用于 10 至 200 km 的长距离。

text.en: Why does single-mode go farther? In multimode, light on different paths covers different distances, so a light pulse sent out at one moment is **spread out** by the time it reaches the far end. The longer the distance, the more it spreads, until consecutive pulses blur together and 1 and 0 cannot be told apart. Single-mode has only one path, so the pulse keeps its shape and goes farther. The slides’ vague line “light cannot even bounce” means exactly this.
text.zh: 为什么单模传得远？多模里，不同路径的光走的路程不一样，同时发出的一个光脉冲，到对面时就被**拉宽**了。距离越长，拉得越宽，前后两个脉冲糊在一起，分不清 1 和 0。单模只有一条路，脉冲不变形，所以传得远。课件那句含糊的『光连弹都不能弹』，指的就是这个意思。

title.en: Fibre in reality: joints, fibre rings, and the bandwidth ceiling
title.zh: 光纤在现实里：接头、光纤环，和带宽的天花板

text.en: How fibres are joined, and how much is lost
text.zh: 光纤怎么接，损失多少

rows.en: Equipment patch cords, places that are plugged and unplugged often
rows.zh: 设备跳线，经常要插拔的地方

rows.en: Aligns and fixes two fibres together
Permanent, melts two fibres into one
Long-distance trunk lines, laid once and left alone
rows.zh: 长距离干线，一次铺好不再动

text.en: Losses add up place by place: on a line of tens of kilometres, the more joints there are, the weaker the light that reaches the far end, until the detector cannot tell 1 from 0. So the longer the trunk line, the more it should use low-loss fusion splices; places that need plugging and unplugging have to put up with the loss of the connector. The caption of the figure on slide 19 says mechanical splice, which does not match the fusion splice listed beside it; go by the text list.
text.zh: 损耗会一处处累加：一条几十千米的线上，接点越多，对端收到的光越弱，弱到探测器认不出 1 和 0。所以越是长距离的干线，越要用损耗小的熔接；需要拆装的地方，只能忍受插头的损耗。课件第 19 页的图注写着 mechanical splice，与旁边列的熔接并不对应，以文字列表为准。

text.en: Fibre rings: why light is turned into electricity and back into light
text.zh: 光纤环：为什么光要变成电再变回光

text.en: The usual shapes of fibre networks are ring and star (recall the topologies of lesson 1). Each device on a ring connects through an **interface**, which has three things in it: an **optical receiver** (a photodiode, light to electricity), a **signal regenerator** (a circuit that cleans up the signal) and an **optical transmitter** (an LED, electricity to light).
text.zh: 光纤网常见的形状是环型和星型（回忆第 1 课的拓扑）。环上每台设备接一个**接口**，接口里有三样东西：**光接收器**（光电二极管，光变电）、**信号再生器**（电路，整理信号）、**光发送器**（LED，电变光）。

text.en: Why turn light into electricity and then back into light? Because the interface has two jobs: hand the data meant for itself to the computer; and **regenerate** other people’s data, that is, clean up the weakened, distorted signal and pass it on to the next stop. Cleaning up and deciding are easiest at the electrical level. This is the physical form of the ring topology in lesson 1, “each device takes in the previous one’s data and passes it to the next”, and it also shows what a ring is afraid of: if one device fails, the ring is broken.
text.zh: 为什么要把光变成电、再变回光？因为接口要做两件事：把发给自己的数据交给电脑；把别人的数据**再生**，也就是整理变弱、变形的信号，再接着往下一站发。整理和判断在电这一级最容易做。这正是第 1 课里环型拓扑『每台收下前一台的数据，再转给下一台』的物理模样，也说明了环型怕什么：一台设备出故障，环就断了。

text.en: Three wired media side by side
text.zh: 三种有线介质并排看

rows.en: About 16 MHz to 2 GHz, depending on grade
rows.zh: 约 16 MHz 至 2 GHz，看线的等级

rows.en: About 100 m per Ethernet segment (telephone lines can go farther)
rows.zh: 以太网一段约 100 m（电话线可以更远）

rows.en: Multimode a few hundred metres, single-mode 10 to 200 km
rows.zh: 多模几百米，单模 10 至 200 km

rows.en: The fibre itself is cheap; equipment and installation usually cost more
rows.zh: 线本身不贵，设备和施工通常更贵

summary.en: Why bandwidth has grown faster than CPUs
summary.zh: 带宽为什么涨得比 CPU 还快

text.en: Slide 10 compares two curves. The CPU went from 4.77 MHz in 1981 to about 6 GHz in 2026: 6000 ÷ 4.77 ≈ 1260 times. Bandwidth went from 0.3 kbps in 1981 to 10 Gbps for consumer fibre: $10^{10} \div 300 \approx 3.3 \times 10^{7}$, about 33 million times, and in data centres up to 1.6 Tbps.
text.zh: 课件第 10 页对比了两条曲线。CPU 从 1981 年的 4.77 MHz，涨到 2026 年约 6 GHz：6000 ÷ 4.77 ≈ 1260 倍。带宽从 1981 年的 0.3 kbps，涨到消费级光纤的 10 Gbps：$10^{10} \div 300 \approx 3.3 \times 10^{7}$，约 3300 万倍，数据中心更到 1.6 Tbps。

text.en: Why has bandwidth grown faster? CPUs rely on etching circuits into silicon, and have hit a wall as they run too hot and the lines approach physical limits. On the fibre side the capacity of the glass thread itself is still huge: experimental fibres have exceeded 400 Tbps. What holds things back is the two ends: the speed at which we turn electrical bits into light pulses (and back). So the bottleneck is not the fibre but the conversion between electricity and light.
text.zh: 为什么带宽涨得更快？CPU 靠在硅片上刻电路，快到发热、线条细到物理极限，已经撞墙。光纤这边，玻璃丝本身的容量还大得很：实验光纤已经超过 400 Tbps。卡住的是两头：我们把电信号的比特变成光脉冲（以及变回来）的速度。所以瓶颈不在光纤，而在电与光的转换。

title.en: Choose a medium for a backbone link
title.zh: 给骨干链路选介质

prompt.en: Between two cities 150 km apart, a backbone link needing extremely high bandwidth is to be laid. Which medium is most suitable?
prompt.zh: 要在相距 150 km 的两座城市之间，铺一条需要极高带宽的骨干链路。哪种介质最合适？

label.en: Twisted pair, with repeaters every so often
label.zh: 双绞线，每隔一段加中继器

feedback.en: Twisted pair has limited bandwidth, and attenuation grows with frequency. 150 km would need far too many repeaters, and still could not support the bandwidth a backbone needs.
feedback.zh: 双绞线的带宽有限，而且频率越高衰减越大。150 km 要放太多中继器，也撑不起骨干要的带宽。

label.en: Multimode fibre, with LEDs
label.zh: 多模光纤，配 LED

feedback.en: Multimode fibre suits only short distances of a few hundred metres: light takes many paths and the pulse spreads, so over 150 km it would long since have smeared into one.
feedback.zh: 多模光纤只适合几百米的短距离：光走多条路，脉冲被拉宽，150 km 早糊成一片了。

label.en: Single-mode fibre, with a laser
label.zh: 单模光纤，配激光

label.en: GEO satellite
label.zh: GEO 卫星

feedback.en: A satellite’s bandwidth is limited, and a single hop already has a delay of about 0.24 s, so it does not suit a high-capacity trunk.
feedback.zh: 卫星的带宽有限，单跳延迟就有约 0.24 秒，不适合做大容量干线。

explain.en: Far and needing large bandwidth: choose single-mode fibre with a laser. The core is thin, so the pulse is not spread, and it works over 10 to 200 km; the glass thread has THz-scale bandwidth and very little signal loss.
explain.zh: 又远又要大带宽，选单模光纤配激光：纤芯细，脉冲不被拉宽，10 至 200 km 都能走；玻璃丝的带宽是 THz 量级，信号损失还很小。

title.en: Wireless: electromagnetic waves, wavelength times frequency equals the speed of light
title.zh: 无线：电磁波，波长乘频率等于光速

text.en: Phones and laptops need to **move**, which a wire cannot tie down. Wireless networks share a common foundation: the propagation of **electromagnetic waves**. A wireless signal is **broadcast** over an area, so transmissions can collide, and rules are needed to manage them.
text.zh: 手机、笔记本需要**移动**，这是线拴不住的。无线网络有共同的基础：**电磁波** (electromagnetic wave) 的传播。无线信号是向一片区域**广播**出去的，所以会碰撞，需要规则来管理。

text.en: First meet the three quantities of an electromagnetic wave. **Frequency**: how many times it oscillates per second, in hertz (Hz). **Wavelength**: the distance between two adjacent crests (or troughs). **Speed**: all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed, the speed of light, about $3\times 10^{8}$ m/s. The basic relation among the three is:
text.zh: 先认识电磁波的三个量。**频率** (frequency)：每秒振荡多少次，单位赫兹 (Hz)。**波长** (wavelength)：相邻两个波峰（或波谷）之间的距离。**速度**：所有电磁波速度一样，都是光速，约 $3\times 10^{8}$ m/s。三者的基本关系是：

text.en: Check the units: (m) × (1/s) = (m/s). The higher the frequency, the shorter the wavelength.
text.zh: 单位对一下：（m）×（1/s）=（m/s）。频率越高，波长越短。

caption.en: How to read the spectrum chart on slide 23
caption.zh: 课件第 23 页的频谱图怎么读

text.en: The chart on slide 23 can be read in three layers. Upper layer: the whole spectrum, from low to high: radio, microwave, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet... Lower layer: a magnified section, marking where various things fall. The bottom row LF, MF, HF, VHF, UHF, SHF, EHF, THF are abbreviations of the **bands**, that is Low, Medium, High, Very High, Ultra High, Super High, Extremely High, Tremendously High Frequency, each ten times higher than the one before.
text.zh: 课件第 23 页的图，看三层就够了。上层：整个频谱，从低到高依次是无线电、微波、红外、可见光、紫外……下层：放大了其中一段，标出各种东西落在哪里。最底下一排 LF、MF、HF、VHF、UHF、SHF、EHF、THF 是**波段**的缩写，就是 Low、Medium、High、Very High、Ultra High、Super High、Extremely High、Tremendously High Frequency，每一档比前一档高 10 倍。

text.en: Different bands behave differently: radio is used for wide-area broadcasting; microwave for local networks and 3G/4G; infrared and light travel only by **line of sight**. The higher the frequency, the shorter the wavelength and the more it is like light: the more it travels in a straight line and the more easily walls and rain block it.
text.zh: 不同的波段性质不同：无线电用于大范围的广播；微波用于局域网和 3G/4G；红外和光只能**视线传播** (line-of-sight)。频率越高，波长越短，就越像光：越是沿直线走，越容易被墙和雨挡住。

text.en: How exactly are the “rules” managed? Broadly two ways. One is **licensing**: the government assigns certain bands to a particular operator for exclusive use, such as mobile phone networks. The other is **unlicensed bands**: anyone can use them but must share, and devices have to be polite, such as the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz commonly used by Wi-Fi. A Wi-Fi device listens before sending to see whether anyone else is transmitting; that method is left to lesson 7.
text.zh: 『需要管理规则』具体怎么管？大体两种办法。一是**许可**：政府把某些频段批给某个运营商专用，例如手机网络。二是**免许可频段**：谁都可以用，但必须共享，设备得守礼貌，例如 Wi-Fi 常用的 2.4 GHz 和 5 GHz。Wi-Fi 设备发之前先听一听有没有人在发，这个办法留到第 7 课。

text.en: Wireless versus wired
text.zh: 无线与有线

rows.en: Naturally supports mobility and broadcast; cheap and easy to deploy
rows.zh: 天然支持移动和广播；部署便宜、容易

rows.en: Transmissions interfere with each other and must be managed; signal strength and rate fluctuate a lot
rows.zh: 传输互相干扰，要管理；信号强度和速率波动很大

rows.en: Easy to keep a fixed rate; supports point-to-point
rows.zh: 容易保持固定的速率；支持点对点

rows.en: Expensive to lay, especially over long distances; supports neither mobility nor broadcast
rows.zh: 铺设贵，尤其是长距离；不支持移动，也不支持广播

title.en: The wavelength of 2.4 GHz
title.zh: 2.4 GHz 的波长

prompt.en: Wi-Fi commonly uses 2.4 GHz. Taking the speed of electromagnetic waves as $3\times 10^{8}$ m/s, what is the wavelength at this frequency, in metres?
prompt.zh: Wi-Fi 常用 2.4 GHz。电磁波的速度取 $3\times 10^{8}$ m/s，这个频率的波长是多少米？

hints.en: Wavelength = speed of light ÷ frequency. First convert GHz to Hz: 1 GHz = $10^{9}$ Hz.
hints.zh: 波长 = 光速 ÷ 频率。先把 GHz 换成 Hz：1 GHz = $10^{9}$ Hz。

explain.en: λ = (3×10^8) ÷ (2.4×10^9) = 0.125 m, that is 12.5 cm. At 5 GHz the wavelength is only 0.06 m: higher frequency, shorter wavelength, more easily blocked by walls.
explain.zh: λ = (3×10^8) ÷ (2.4×10^9) = 0.125 m，也就是 12.5 cm。如果换成 5 GHz，波长只有 0.06 m：频率更高，波长更短，更容易被墙挡住。

title.en: Satellites: altitude decides delay and number
title.zh: 卫星：高度决定延迟和数量

text.en: Satellites are good at two things: **broadcasting** to a large area, and communicating **anywhere, anytime** (once a satellite is launched, communication can be set up anywhere very quickly). By altitude there are three kinds, and different altitudes have completely different properties.
text.zh: 卫星擅长两件事：向大片区域**广播**，以及**随时随地**通信（卫星发射之后，可以很快在任何地方建立通信）。按高度分三类，高度不同，性质完全不同。

alt.en: The vertical axis is altitude: GEO about 35,800 km, MEO about 10,000 km between the two Van Allen belts, LEO a few hundred km close to the ground
alt.zh: 纵轴是高度：GEO 约 35,800 km，MEO 约 10,000 km，在两条范艾伦带之间，LEO 几百 km 贴近地面

caption.en: Schematic; altitudes are not exactly to scale. The Van Allen belts are regions of strong particle radiation that satellites must avoid
caption.zh: 示意图，高度不按精确比例；范艾伦带是粒子辐射很强的区域，卫星要避开

text.en: The slides do not say whether the delay is one-way or round trip. Counting one hop “ground station, satellite, ground station”: the path is about twice the altitude, and time = path ÷ speed of light, and the results all fall within the ranges the slides give. GEO comes out at 0.24 s while the slides say 270 ms; the extra is because a satellite not directly overhead has a longer slant path, plus equipment processing.
text.zh: 课件的延迟没说是单程还是往返。按『地面站、卫星、地面站』这一跳来算：路程约是高度的 2 倍，时间 = 路程 ÷ 光速，算出来都落在课件给的范围里。GEO 算出 0.24 s，课件写 270 ms，多出来的是卫星不在正上方时斜线更长，再加设备处理。

text.en: A GEO satellite goes round the Earth once in exactly 24 hours, so it always hangs above the same point on the ground, and a ground antenna aimed once never needs to move again. LEO is much lower with a small delay, but it moves so fast that one satellite passes overhead in a few minutes, so many satellites are needed to relay.
text.zh: GEO 卫星绕地球一圈正好 24 小时，所以始终悬在地面同一点的上空，地面天线对准一次就不用再动。LEO 低得多，延迟小，但绕得飞快，一颗卫星几分钟就飞过头顶，所以要很多颗接力。

title.en: 50 and 1584 do not contradict
title.zh: 50 颗和 1584 颗，不矛盾

body.en: The table says LEO needs 50 satellites for global coverage, while Starlink’s first shell alone has 1584 (72 orbits, 22 satellites each, at 550 km). The former is “the fewest satellites such that any point on Earth sees at least one at any moment”, which is only about coverage. Starlink needs more than coverage: it must give many users **capacity** (each satellite’s bandwidth is limited, so with more people the satellites must be packed denser so that several share the load), and **continuous service** (LEO satellites fly away fast, so the next one must take over). So the number is far larger.
body.zh: 表里说 LEO 全球覆盖需要 50 颗，星链第一层就有 1584 颗（72 条轨道，每条 22 颗，高度 550 km）。前者是『最少几颗，才能让地球上任何一点任何时刻至少看见一颗』，只管覆盖。星链要的不只是覆盖：要给很多用户提供**容量**（每颗卫星的带宽有限，人多了就得把卫星布得更密，让多颗一起分担），还要**连续服务**（LEO 卫星很快飞走，必须有下一颗接上）。所以数目大得多。

title.en: Beyond the slides
title.zh: 超出课件

body.en: Slide 25 rounds the GEO altitude to 35,000 km and slide 26 writes 35,800 km; they mean the same altitude. The more accurate value is about 35,786 km.
body.zh: 第 25 页把 GEO 高度取整写成 35,000 km，第 26 页写 35,800 km，说的是同一个高度；更准确的值约是 35,786 km。

summary.en: The arrows 1 to 4 in the VSAT figure
summary.zh: VSAT 图里的 1 至 4 号箭头

text.en: VSAT (Very Small Aperture Terminal) is a small-dish satellite terminal. For two VSATs to communicate, they go through a **hub**: the terminal uploads data to the GEO satellite (1), the satellite passes it to the hub (2), the hub processes it and uploads it to the satellite again (3), and the satellite delivers it to the other terminal (4). One trip makes 4 up/down hops, and light alone takes nearly 0.5 s on the way. The bands used, L, S, C, Ku and Ka, are all measured in GHz; some are crowded and some fear rain: the higher the frequency, the more rain affects the signal.
text.zh: VSAT (Very Small Aperture Terminal) 是小口径的卫星终端。两个 VSAT 要通信，要经过一个**枢纽** (hub)：终端把数据上传给 GEO 卫星（1），卫星转给枢纽（2），枢纽处理后再上传给卫星（3），卫星再送到另一个终端（4）。一来一回走了 4 个上下行，光在路上就要将近 0.5 秒。使用的 L、S、C、Ku、Ka 都是以 GHz 计的频段，有的拥挤，有的怕下雨：频率越高，雨对信号的影响越大。

text.en: Which to choose for which case
text.zh: 什么场景选什么

rows.en: Broadcasting TV signals to a large region
rows.zh: 向大片地区广播电视信号

rows.en: One covers a large area, and users’ antennas just point at it, fixed
rows.zh: 一颗盖住一大片，用户的天线固定对准就行

rows.en: Internet at sea, in the wilderness or on a plane
rows.zh: 海上、荒野、飞机上要上网

rows.en: Satellite (LEO if you want low delay)
There is simply no way to lay a line

rows.zh: 城市之间的大容量干线
长距离上有巨大的带宽

rows.en: A trade-off: fibre has large bandwidth but is hard to lay; satellites are easy to set up but have limited bandwidth
rows.zh: 要权衡：光纤带宽大但难铺，卫星好建但带宽有限

rows.en: Compare the cost per household with the bandwidth needed
rows.zh: 比较每户的成本和需要的带宽

rows.en: Restoring communication right after a disaster
No construction needed; once launched, a satellite can quickly set up communication anywhere
rows.zh: 不用施工，卫星发射之后能快速在任何地方建立通信

title.en: How long does one hop via a GEO satellite take
title.zh: 经 GEO 卫星一跳要多久

prompt.en: A signal leaves the ground station, goes up to a GEO satellite (altitude 35,800 km), and comes back down to a ground station. Take both the uplink and downlink paths as approximately the satellite’s altitude, and the signal speed as 300 000 km/s. How many seconds does this hop take? (Round to two decimals.)
prompt.zh: 信号从地面站出发，上行到 GEO 卫星（高度 35,800 km），再下行回地面站。上行、下行的路程都近似取卫星的高度，信号速度取 300 000 km/s。这一跳要多少秒？（保留两位小数）

hints.zh: 路程 = 高度 × 2；时间 = 路程 ÷ 速度。

explain.en: 2×35,800 ÷ 300,000 ≈ 0.239 s, about 0.24 s. For “request plus reply” there are two hops, about 0.48 s. GEO internet feels “laggy” mainly because it is limited by the speed of light and the 36,000 km distance, not by small bandwidth. By comparison, for LEO at 550 km a hop takes only about 3.7 ms.
explain.zh: 2×35,800 ÷ 300,000 ≈ 0.239 s，约 0.24 s。如果是『请求加回复』，要两跳，约 0.48 s。GEO 上网觉得『卡』，主要是被光速和 3.6 万公里的距离限制，不是带宽小。对比一下，550 km 的 LEO，一跳只要约 3.7 ms。

title.en: How many knobs a signal has
title.zh: 信号上有几个旋钮

prompt.en: To send 0s and 1s over a wire, you have a sine signal that oscillates up and down, $f(t) = A\sin(2\pi f t + \varphi)$. To make it carry information, what can you change in it?
prompt.zh: 要用一根线传 0 和 1，你手上有一个会上下振荡的正弦信号 $f(t) = A\sin(2\pi f t + \varphi)$。想让它带上信息，你能去改它的什么？

label.en: Only the amplitude A
label.zh: 只能改幅度 A

feedback.en: Amplitude is only one of them. There is more than one way to change a signal.
feedback.zh: 幅度只是其中一个。改信号的办法不止一种。

label.en: A, f and φ can all be changed, and each can be used to carry information
label.zh: A、f、φ 三个量都可以改，每一个都能用来携带信息

label.en: Only the frequency f; the rest is fixed
label.zh: 只能改频率 f，其余是固定的

feedback.en: Frequency is only one of the three knobs; amplitude and phase can be changed as well.
feedback.zh: 频率只是三个旋钮之一，幅度和相位同样可以改。

explain.en: A sine wave has three knobs: amplitude A, frequency f and phase φ. Next we see what each is, and then how to use them to represent 0 and 1.
explain.zh: 正弦波有三个旋钮：幅度 A、频率 f、相位 φ。下面看它们各是什么，再看怎样用它们来表示 0 和 1。

title.en: The sine wave: three knobs
title.zh: 正弦波：三个旋钮

text.en: Information on a wire travels by changing some physical quantity: voltage or current (for light and radio waves, light intensity or the electromagnetic field). The most basic “thing that changes” is the sine wave:
text.zh: 线上传信息，靠的是改变某个物理量：电压、电流（光和无线电波则是光强、电磁场）。最基本的『会变的东西』，是正弦波：

items.en: **A**: amplitude, how tall the wave is.
**f**: frequency, how many oscillations per second, in Hz.
items.zh: **f**：频率 (frequency)，每秒振荡几次，单位 Hz。

items.en: **φ**: phase, where the wave starts, that is, how far the whole wave is shifted left or right.
items.zh: **φ**：相位 (phase)，波从哪里起头，也就是整个波往左或往右挪了多少。

text.en: The time for one oscillation is called the **period** $T = \dfrac{1}{f}$. Example: when $f = 1000$ Hz, $T = 1$ ms.
text.zh: 振荡一次要的时间叫**周期** $T = \dfrac{1}{f}$。例：$f = 1000$ Hz 时，$T = 1$ ms。

alt.en: Three sets of waveforms: changing amplitude, the blue wave is taller than the grey one; changing frequency, the blue wave is denser than the grey one; changing phase, the blue wave is shifted a little to the left as a whole
alt.zh: 三组波形：改幅度，蓝波比灰波高；改频率，蓝波比灰波密；改相位，蓝波比灰波整体向左挪了一点

caption.en: Change any one of the three quantities and the waveform changes
caption.zh: 改变三个量中的任何一个，波形就变了

text.en: Whichever of the three is changed, the waveform changes. The sender changes it, the receiver sees the change, and so can tell “what was sent”. Mapping 0 and 1 to different values of the three knobs is the **modulation** on the next page.
text.zh: 这三个量，改了哪一个，波形就变了。发送方改它，接收方看出变化，就能认出『发的是什么』。把 0 和 1 对应到这三个旋钮的不同取值，就是下一页的**调制**。

title.en: Modulation: putting bits on a suitable frequency
title.zh: 调制：把比特放到合适的频率上

text.en: Bits are 0 and 1, but what travels on a wire is a wave. Turning bits into a signal that can travel on the wire is called **modulation**. There are two approaches.
text.zh: 比特是 0 和 1，线上要走的是波。把比特变成能在线上走的信号，叫**调制** (modulation)。有两种思路。

items.en: **Baseband transmission**: the signal occupies a frequency range **starting at 0 and going up to some highest frequency**. Example: voice in the telephone system, occupying 0 to 4 kHz.
items.zh: **基带传输** (baseband)：信号占的频率范围**从 0 开始，到某个最高频率**。例：电话系统里的语音，占 0 到 4 kHz。

items.en: **Passband transmission**: the signal is **shifted to a higher frequency range**. Example: ADSL.
items.zh: **通带传输** (passband)：把信号**搬到更高的频率范围**去。例：ADSL。

text.en: Why shift to high frequency
text.zh: 为什么要搬到高频

text.en: There are two practical reasons. First, **several users share one wire**: on your home phone line, voice already occupies 0 to 4 kHz. If data used that range too, it would have to fight with calls. Shifting data above 26 kHz, the two each take a stretch and do not disturb each other, so you can be on the phone and online at the same time. Second, **a channel lets only part of the frequencies through**: many channels (radio, fibre) pass only a certain range of frequencies smoothly, and a signal must fall within that range to be sent out and received.
text.zh: 有两个现实的原因。第一，**多个用户共用一根线**：你家的电话线上，语音已经占了 0 至 4 kHz。数据如果也用这一段，就得和打电话抢。把数据搬到 26 kHz 以上，两者各占一段，互不打扰，所以可以一边打电话一边上网。第二，**信道只放行一部分频率**：很多信道（无线电、光纤）只让某一段频率顺利通过，信号必须落在那一段里，才发得出去、收得到。

caption.en: On the same phone line, voice and data each take a range of frequencies
caption.zh: 同一根电话线，语音和数据各占一段频率

text.en: The two ranges 4 to 26 kHz and 108 to 138 kHz in the figure are deliberately left empty, and are called **guard bands**. A filter cannot cut with a single clean edge, and adjacent ranges always leak a little, so leaving a gap keeps them from interfering. Downstream (138 to 1104 kHz) is much wider than upstream: when browsing, downloads always exceed uploads.
text.zh: 图里 4 至 26 kHz、108 至 138 kHz 两段故意空着，叫**保护带** (guard band)。滤波器不可能一刀切，相邻的两段总有一点泄漏，空开才不互相干扰。下行（138 至 1104 kHz）比上行宽得多：看网页，下载的总比上传的多。

text.en: Putting bits on a carrier
text.zh: 把比特放到载波上

text.en: In passband, there is first a fixed high-frequency sine wave called the **carrier**, which carries no information by itself. The sender changes one knob of the carrier to represent 0 and 1. Below is how the same bit string 1 0 1 1 0 0 1 0 looks in baseband **NRZ** (non-return-to-zero: 1 is a high level, 0 a low level) and in three passband ways.
text.zh: 通带里，先有一个固定的高频正弦波，叫**载波** (carrier)，它自己不带信息。发送方改载波的一个旋钮，来表示 0 和 1。下面是同一串比特 1 0 1 1 0 0 1 0，在基带的 **NRZ**（不归零码 non-return-to-zero：1 用高电平，0 用低电平）和三种通带方式里的样子。

alt.en: Four ways to draw the same bit string 1 0 1 1 0 0 1 0: NRZ is a square wave; in amplitude shift keying 1 has a wave and 0 has none; in frequency shift keying 1 is a dense wave and 0 a sparse one; in phase shift keying 1 and 0 have the same frequency but are upside-down versions of each other
alt.zh: 同一串比特 1 0 1 1 0 0 1 0 的四种画法：NRZ 的方波；幅移键控里 1 有波、0 没有波；频移键控里 1 是密波、0 是疏波；相移键控里 1 和 0 的波频率一样但上下相反

caption.en: Slide 34: the same bit string, four signals
caption.zh: 课件第 34 页：同一串比特，四种信号

rows.zh: 幅移键控 (ASK, amplitude shift keying)

rows.en: No wave, or a very small one
Simplest; but noise interferes directly with the amplitude, so it is generally the least noise-resistant
rows.zh: 最简单；但噪声直接干扰幅度，一般抗噪最差
频移键控 (FSK, frequency shift keying)

rows.en: Better against amplitude noise, takes a wider band
rows.zh: 抗幅度噪声好一些，要占更宽的频带
相移键控 (PSK, phase shift keying)

text.en: How does the receiver read it? By looking at the received wave: whether it is there, whether it is dense or sparse, whether it has flipped, it can tell 0 from 1. This answers the two questions on slide 35: the receiver recognizes a signal by a “difference agreed in advance”; in every example above there are only **two** kinds of signal (two amplitudes, or two frequencies, or two phases), so one signal unit carries 1 bit. With more kinds of signal, one unit can carry several bits, as in symbol rate later.
text.zh: 接收方怎么读？看收到的波：有没有、是密还是疏、翻没翻个儿，就能认出 0 和 1。这正好回答课件第 35 页的两个问题：接收方靠『事先约好的区别』来认信号；上面每个例子里都只有**两种**信号（两种幅度，或两种频率，或两种相位），所以一个信号单元带 1 个比特。信号的种类多了，一个单元就能带多个比特，见后面的码元速率。

title.en: How a phone call and internet share one wire
title.zh: 电话和上网怎样共用一根线

prompt.en: On a phone line, voice occupies 0 to 4 kHz. ADSL wants to send data on the same wire as well, while people can still make calls at the same time. Which of the following is most sensible?
prompt.zh: 一根电话线上，语音占 0 至 4 kHz。ADSL 要在同一根线上再传数据，并且人们还能同时打电话。下面哪种做法最合理？

label.en: Data also uses baseband, taking 0 to 4 kHz, taking turns with voice
label.zh: 数据也用基带，占 0 至 4 kHz，和语音轮流使用

feedback.en: Taking turns means you cannot be on the phone and online at once; and data and voice squeezed into the same range of frequencies would interfere.
feedback.zh: 轮流使用，就不能一边打电话一边上网了；而且数据和语音挤在同一段频率里会互相干扰。

label.en: Modulate the data into a passband above 26 kHz, apart from the voice band
label.zh: 把数据调制到 26 kHz 以上的通带，和语音的频段错开

label.en: Turn the voice volume up to drown the data
label.zh: 把语音的音量调大，盖过数据

feedback.en: Two signals mixed in the same range of frequencies cannot be separated; a louder volume only makes it worse.
feedback.zh: 两路信号混在同一段频率里没法分开，音量大只会更糟。

label.en: Put the data at frequencies below 0 Hz
label.zh: 把数据放在 0 Hz 以下的频率

feedback.en: There are no usable frequencies below 0 Hz. To stay apart from voice, you can only shift upward.
feedback.zh: 没有 0 Hz 以下可用的频率。要和语音错开，只能往上搬。

explain.en: To share one wire, let different signals take different frequencies: voice stays in baseband 0 to 4 kHz, and data is modulated into a higher passband, with upstream and downstream each taking a range and guard bands in between.
explain.zh: 要共用一根线，就让不同的信号占不同的频率：语音留在基带 0 至 4 kHz，数据被调制到更高的通带，上下行各占一段，中间留保护带。

title.en: How many looks per second
title.zh: 每秒要看几次

prompt.en: The receiver wants to record a 1000 Hz sine wave by “measuring the voltage every short interval” and then reconstruct it. At least how many measurements per second are needed to avoid a wrong reconstruction?
prompt.zh: 接收方要把一个 1000 Hz 的正弦波，用『每隔一小段时间量一次电压』的办法记下来，再还原。每秒至少要量多少次，才不会还原错？

label.en: 1000: the wave oscillates 1000 times a second, so 1000 measurements is just right
label.zh: 1000 次：波每秒振 1000 次，量 1000 次正好

feedback.en: Measuring once per oscillation might land on the same position every time, looking like a straight line, and you could not tell it was swinging.
feedback.zh: 每次振荡只量一次，可能每次都量在同一个位置，看上去就像一条直线，分不清它在摆动。

label.en: 2000 or more: at least two measurements in each oscillation
label.zh: 2000 次以上：每次振荡里至少量两次

label.en: 500 is enough, a sine wave is simple
label.zh: 500 次就够，正弦波很简单

feedback.en: A simple waveform does not mean fewer measurements. With less than one measurement per oscillation you only get a wrong, slow wave.
feedback.zh: 波形简单不等于可以少量。每次振荡要量不到一次，只会得到一条错误的慢波。

explain.en: The answer is b. The next page explains why “twice” and what happens when you measure too sparsely.
explain.zh: 答案是 b。下一页说为什么是『两倍』，以及量得太稀会出什么事。

title.en: Sampling: at least twice the highest frequency
title.zh: 采样：至少要两倍于最高频率

text.en: What the receiver gets is a continuously varying wave on the wire (an analog signal), while a computer processes a string of numbers. In between comes **sampling**: measuring once every short interval $T_s$ to get a string of samples. The sampling rate $f_s = \dfrac{1}{T_s}$ is how many measurements per second. To reconstruct, the samples are joined back into a wave.
text.zh: 接收方拿到的是线上连续变化的波（模拟信号），而计算机处理的是一串数字。中间要经过**采样** (sampling)：每隔一小段时间 $T_s$ 量一次，得到一串样本。采样率 $f_s = \dfrac{1}{T_s}$，就是每秒量几次。想还原的时候，再把样本连成波。

text.en: Measure too sparsely and trouble follows.
text.zh: 量得太稀，就会出事。

alt.en: Left: the sampling rate is twice the signal frequency, the samples fall on peaks and troughs, and joined up they recover a wave of the same period; right: the sampling rate is only two thirds of the signal frequency, and three samples join into a wave of much lower frequency that is wrong
alt.zh: 左：采样率是信号频率的两倍，样本落在波峰和波谷，连起来还原出同样周期的波；右：采样率只有信号频率的三分之二，三个样本连成一条频率低得多的错误的波

caption.en: Grey line: original signal; red dots: samples; blue dashed line: wave rebuilt from the samples
caption.zh: 灰线：原信号；红点：样本；蓝虚线：用样本重建的波

text.en: For perfect reconstruction, the sampling rate must be at least twice the **highest frequency** in the signal:
text.zh: 要完美还原，采样率必须至少是信号里**最高频率**的两倍：

text.en: $f_H$ is the highest frequency appearing in the original signal. This is the conclusion of **Nyquist**. Why “twice”? One oscillation has one crest and one trough. You need to catch at least one peak and one trough in each oscillation to know it is swinging up and down; with only one point, you cannot tell whether it is swinging or sitting still. Exactly twice is the boundary case; in practice go slightly above twice.
text.zh: $f_H$ 是原信号里出现的最高频率。这就是**奈奎斯特** (Nyquist) 的结论。为什么是『两倍』？一次振荡里有一个波峰、一个波谷。至少要在每次振荡里量到一次峰、一次谷，才知道它在上下摆动；只量一个点，你分不清它是在摆动，还是停在原地。恰好等于两倍是边界情形，实际要略高于两倍。

text.en: What happens if you do not measure enough? Look at the right of the figure: the sampling rate is only $\frac{2}{3}f_0$, and joining the samples gives a **wrong wave of much lower frequency**. This false wave that appears from under-sampling is called **aliasing**: the original high-frequency wave poses as a low-frequency one in the samples’ eyes, and afterwards it can never be told apart.
text.zh: 量得不够会怎样？看图右：采样率只有 $\frac{2}{3}f_0$，把样本连起来，得到的是一条**频率低得多的错误的波**。这种因采样不足而冒出来的假波，叫**混叠** (aliasing)：原来的高频波，在样本眼里冒充成了低频波，事后再也分不出来。

text.en: A real number: telephone voice has a highest frequency of about 4 kHz, so it must be sampled at least 8000 times per second. Digital telephony samples exactly 8000 times per second, recording each with 8 bits: 8000 × 8 = 64 000 bit/s, the 64 kbit/s mentioned earlier.
text.zh: 一个真实的数字：电话语音最高约 4 kHz，所以每秒至少采样 8000 次。数字电话正是每秒采样 8000 次，每次用 8 比特记下来：8000 × 8 = 64 000 bit/s，也就是前面说的 64 kbit/s。

text.en: Relation to the previous page: modulation is the sender turning bits into waves; the receiver, to recover bits from the received wave, must first turn the wave into samples. With sampling done right, the original wave can be reconstructed, and then you decide which amplitude, frequency or phase each bit used.
text.zh: 和前一页的关系：调制是发送方把比特变成波；接收方要从收到的波里恢复比特，要先把波变成样本。采样对了，才能还原出原来的波，再去判断每个比特放的是哪种幅度、频率或相位。

title.en: Symbol rate: one signal change can carry several bits
title.zh: 码元速率：一次信号变化，可以带几个比特

text.en: So far each signal unit, a **symbol**, carries just 1 bit: two states, corresponding to 0 and 1. But a symbol can have more states and carry several bits at a time.
text.zh: 前面每个信号单元，也就是一个**码元** (symbol)，只带 1 个比特：两种状态，对应 0 和 1。但一个码元可以有更多种状态，一次带多个比特。

text.en: Say the signal has $V$ different values (levels, amplitudes, frequencies or phases). Each symbol picks one of the $V$, so it distinguishes $V$ cases and can carry $\log_2 V$ bits: 2 values carry 1 bit, 4 carry 2 bits, 8 carry 3 bits.
text.zh: 设信号有 $V$ 种不同的取值（电平、幅度、频率或相位）。每个码元要从 $V$ 种里选一种，能区分 $V$ 种情况，所以能带 $\log_2 V$ 个比特：2 种带 1 比特，4 种带 2 比特，8 种带 3 比特。

text.en: The **symbol rate** (also called the baud rate) is how many times per second the signal changes; the **data rate** is how many bits are sent per second. The two are equal only when $V = 2$.
text.zh: **码元速率** (symbol rate，也叫波特率 baud rate) 是每秒信号变化的次数；**数据速率** (data rate) 是每秒传多少比特。两者只有在 $V = 2$ 时才相等。

alt.en: Left: two levels, 0 V and 3 V, each symbol is 1 bit, so 6 symbols are 6 bits; right: four levels from 0 to 3 V, each symbol is 2 bits, so 6 symbols are 12 bits
alt.zh: 左：两个电平 0 V 和 3 V，每个码元表示 1 个比特，6 个码元是 6 比特；右：四个电平 0 到 3 V，每个码元表示 2 个比特，6 个码元是 12 比特

caption.en: The two figures on slide 37 (the voltage labels in the original are hard to read, so redrawn here)
caption.zh: 课件第 37 页的两张图（电压标注原图看不清，这里重画）

text.en: Work through one step by step. Four levels, changing 1000 times per second (1000 baud):
text.zh: 按步骤算一个。四个电平，每秒变化 1000 次（1000 baud）：

text.en: The speed of signal changes is unchanged, yet the data rate has doubled. With the same 1000 baud and 8 levels, it is 3×1000 = 3000 bit/s. Then why not keep adding levels? The more densely the levels are packed, the more easily noise makes the receiver misread. How much can be sent at most is answered by channel capacity in the next lesson.
text.zh: 信号变化的快慢没变，数据速率却翻了一倍。同样 1000 baud，用 8 个电平，就是 3×1000 = 3000 bit/s。那为什么不一直加电平？电平挤得越密，噪声越容易让接收方认错。最多能传多少，下一课的信道容量会回答。

title.en: The road this lesson has walked
title.zh: 这一课走过的路

body.en: First see the wire as a pipe, keeping only its thickness (bandwidth) and length (delay); then look at what the pipe is made of: copper, light, radio waves, satellites, each with its own attenuation, distance and cost; finally see how bits become the signal in the pipe: modulation puts bits on a suitable frequency, sampling lets the receiver reconstruct, and symbols let one change carry several bits.
body.zh: 先把线看成一根管子，只留粗细（带宽）和长短（延迟）；再看管子的材料：铜、光、电波、卫星，各有各的衰减、距离和代价；最后看比特怎样变成管子里的信号：调制把比特放到合适的频率，采样让接收方还原，码元让一次变化带上多个比特。

title.en: 8 levels, 2400 baud
title.zh: 8 个电平，2400 baud

prompt.en: A signal has 8 different levels and changes 2400 times per second (2400 baud). What is the data rate in bit/s?
prompt.zh: 一个信号有 8 种不同的电平，每秒变化 2400 次（2400 baud）。数据速率是多少 bit/s？

hints.en: With 8 states, how many binary digits are needed to tell them apart?
hints.zh: 8 种状态，要用几位二进制才能区分？

hints.en: Data rate = bits per symbol × symbol rate.
hints.zh: 数据速率 = 每个码元的比特数 × 码元速率。

explain.en: $\log_2 8 = 3$, each symbol carries 3 bits, and data rate = 3 × 2400 = 7200 bit/s. The baud rate is 2400 but the bit rate is 3 times that: this is why the two must not be confused.
explain.zh: $\log_2 8 = 3$，每个码元带 3 比特，数据速率 = 3 × 2400 = 7200 bit/s。波特率是 2400，比特率却是它的 3 倍：这就是两者不能混的原因。
